title: CrapBaselineV2
description: Per-kind baseline schema for the CRAP gate, envelope-shaped. Extends the shared baseline-envelope contract. On disk the rows are grouped under `files` (each path once, each method key on its own line); the previous `rows[]` layout still validates so it reaches the scoring-semantics compat axis, which refuses it with the full-scope re-seed command. Distinct from the legacy crap-baseline.schema.json which used a flat shape.

scoringSemantics.description: Identifier for the per-method coverage-join semantics that produced these rows (Story #4775). Deliberately NOT constrained to the current value here: an old-semantics baseline must reach the gate's compat axis, which fails it closed with an explicit re-baseline command, rather than being rejected with a raw schema error.

provenanceStamped.description: Legacy stamp, no longer written (the persisted row carries no line coordinate to qualify). Accepted only so a baseline from before the grouped layout reaches the scoring-semantics compat axis rather than a raw schema error.

startLine.description: Previous rows[] layout only. The persisted CRAP identity is path::method; startLine lives on scan rows in memory.

anonymous.description: Previous rows[] layout only; an anonymous key is recognisable by its `<anon ` prefix.

coordinateSystem.description: Previous rows[] layout only; it qualified startLine, which the persisted identity no longer carries.

rows.description: In-memory row shape `{ path, method, crap }`, which writers validate before encoding; on disk only the previous layout carries rows[].

files.description: The grouped on-disk layout: canonical path (sorted) to an object of `"<method key>": <crap>` entries (sorted by key). A method key is its scope path — enclosing method segments joined by `/`, ending in its own name — with `#<n>` on a later method that would repeat an earlier key in the same file; an anonymous key is wrapped as `<anon …>`. Identity is path::method; no line number is persisted.
